sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Define health.
questions.answer: A state of physical, mental, social and spiritual well-being.

questions.q: Define mental health.
questions.answer: An optimum level of emotional and behavioural adjustment and harmony between the individual's needs and the environment.

questions.q: Name the four strategies of mental hygiene.
questions.answer: Reality contact, impulse control, self-esteem and positive thoughts.

questions.q: Distinguish self-concept and self-esteem in one line each.
questions.answer: Self-concept is the sum total of awareness about oneself; self-esteem is the evaluative component of the self.

questions.q: Name any four signs of poor mental health.
questions.answer: Disorganised routine, short temper, anxiety, withdrawal, irregular sleep, drug use (any four).

questions.q: Name the four Ayurvedic aspects of lifestyle.
questions.answer: Ahara, Vihara, Achara and Vichara.

questions.q: What is Ritucharya?
questions.answer: Taking food and doing activities in accordance with the seasons.

questions.q: Give any two benefits of exercise.
questions.answer: Increases immunity, excretes toxins, controls heart disease and diabetes, delays ageing (any two).

questions.q: What is an activity schedule?
questions.answer: A structured routine of the 24 hours with activities listed in order of priority and importance.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the Ayurvedic term: (i) right food; (ii) right recreation; (iii) right routine; (iv) right thinking.
questions.answer: (i) Ahara. (ii) Vihara. (iii) Achara. (iv) Vichara.

questions.q: Which strategy is described: (i) realistic appraisal of abilities; (ii) control of impulsive behaviour; (iii) sense of personal adequacy; (iv) thinking that produces love and hope?
questions.answer: (i) Reality contact. (ii) Impulse control. (iii) Self-esteem. (iv) Positive thoughts.

questions.q: Name four time management principles.
questions.answer: Prepare a list of work; prioritise; keep a flexible schedule; set time for exercise and leisure (also uninterrupted periods).

questions.q: Name four things a mentally healthy person has.
questions.answer: Self-satisfaction, accommodative intellect, ability to accept criticism, understanding of others' emotional needs, self-control (any four).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is mental hygiene?
questions.answer: The art of developing, maintaining and promoting behavioural, emotional and social skills to sustain good mental health.

questions.q: Distinguish mental ill-health and mental illness.
questions.answer: Mental ill-health is the absence of positive mental health qualities; mental illness is a broad category of behaviour disorders caused by faulty perception, emotion, thinking and attitude.

questions.q: Why is positive thinking important?
questions.answer: It produces love, joy, hope and optimism, strengthening coping, whereas negative thoughts harm the mind and the endocrine system.

questions.q: What is Dincharya?
questions.answer: The day routine: doing activities at the right time of day, such as rising before sunrise and drinking water first.

questions.q: Why should the toughest task be done first?
questions.answer: Energy is high early, and the easiest task can be kept for later when tired.

questions.q: Why keep a flexible schedule?
questions.answer: To handle unplanned events without stress.

questions.q: Why is leisure time important?
questions.answer: It gives mental and physical rest and a break from routine.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain mental health and the relationship with mental hygiene.
questions.answer: Mental health is optimum emotional and behavioural adjustment; mental hygiene is the set of behavioural, emotional and social skills practised to sustain and promote it.

questions.q: Explain reality contact and impulse control.
questions.answer: Reality contact is a realistic appraisal of one's reactions, emotions and abilities, avoiding disappointments; impulse control is mastery over impulsive behaviour needed for healthy adjustment.

questions.q: Describe the indicators of poor mental health.
questions.answer: Disorganised routine, short temper, aggression, restlessness, appetite and sleep problems, poor relationships, anxiety, negative attitudes, withdrawal, abnormal physiology, drugs and smoking.

questions.q: Describe the Ayurvedic principle of Ahara.
questions.answer: Eat fresh fruits, green vegetables, beans, honey, curd and milk in balanced proportions at fixed times, chew well; vegetarian food is invigorating and prevents disease.

questions.q: Describe Vihara (recreation) and its benefits.
questions.answer: Exercise and morning walks make the body strong, raise immunity, excrete toxins, control heart disease and diabetes, delay ageing; music also helps.

questions.q: Explain any three principles of time management.
questions.answer: Prepare a list of tasks the previous night; prioritise with the toughest first; keep a flexible schedule; plan exercise and leisure time.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the concepts of mental health and hygiene and the strategies to achieve good mental hygiene.
questions.answer: Mental health is harmony between the individual's needs and the environment; mental hygiene is the practice of skills to keep it. Strategies: reality contact, impulse control, self-esteem (self-concept's evaluative part) and positive thoughts, which generate love, joy and hope.

questions.q: Describe the indicators of poor mental health and distinguish mental ill-health from mental illness.
questions.answer: Signs: disorganised routine, temper, aggression, restlessness, sleep and appetite problems, poor relationships, anxiety, negativity, withdrawal, abnormal blood pressure, drugs and smoking. Ill-health is the absence of positive qualities; illness is a disorder from faulty perception, emotion, thinking and attitude.

questions.q: Discuss the Ayurvedic behaviours that sustain good health.
questions.answer: Ahara (balanced fresh food, fixed times), Achara (seasonal and daily routine), Vihara (exercise and recreation) and Vichara (self-satisfaction, criticism acceptance, empathy, self-control, freedom from greed and fear).

questions.q: Describe the strategies for time management.
questions.answer: Make an activity schedule with a list prepared the night before, prioritise tough tasks first, identify uninterrupted periods, be flexible, set aside time for exercise and yoga and plan leisure such as music or gardening.
